newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WICKETKEEPER HEALY ROCKS WEST INDIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WICKETKEEPER HEALY ROCKS WEST INDIES.

text.p: Ian Healy compiled the highest score by an Australian wicketkeeper in test history with a gritty unbeaten 161 to demoralise West Indies in the first test on Saturday.
Healy, playing with his usual mixture of determination and occasional inelegance, steered Australia to a commanding 479 all out on the second day at the Gabba.
Australia fast bowlers Glenn McGrath and Paul Reiffel completed a miserable day for the tourists by removing openers Sherwin Campbell and Robert Samuels in quick succession.
At the close, West Indies were 61 for two, still 418 runs behind . Brian Lara was unbeaten on 19 alongside Carl Hooper on four not out.
Healy, who came to the crease with his side struggling on 196 for five, produced a chanceless innings that featured 20 fours and lasted four minutes shy of six hours.
It was his third test century and eclipsed Rodney Marsh's 132 against New Zealand in Adelaide in 1973-74.

Resuming on 47 not out, Healy faced 250 balls to hold Australia's tail together against a tiring and increasingly impotent bowling attack as the home side added 197 to their overnight total of 282 for five.
Healy combined with all-rounder Steve Waugh to add 142 for the sixth wicket.
Healy resumed his principal role behind the stumps late in the day to take a simple catch to dismiss Samuels for 10.
Courtney Walsh, who removed middle order pair Mark Waugh and Michael Bevan with successive balls on Friday, finished with four for 112 from 35 overs.
Healy, renowned for his fighting qualities as a batsman, described the innings, the first century by a native Queenslander in a test in Brisbane, as the best of his career.
"I am very proud of what I achieved today," he said. "It was a very special moment for me to produce this innings on my home ground in front of my family."
Asked if the innings was typical of his image as a cricketer who performs at his best under pressure, Healy said: "I think that's the way my character is written.

"I am very happy to have that as a characteristic response," said Healy, whose three first-class centuries have all been scored in the test arena, making him the only player in test history to have achieved this unusual distinction.
Late in the day, Australia were further encouraged by the return to the bowling crease of leg-spinner Shane Warne.
Warne, who underwent surgery on the ring finger of his right hand in May, bowled five overs in his first test appearance since the operation.
But there was to be no further celebration for Mark Taylor's side as Lara and Hooper safely negotiated Warne's threat.
